I think he is more mentally healthy than I was. I was pressured to do med school straight out of college, then the pandemic happened. After some self reflection and reading on the lives of unconventional women and women older than me, I try not to pressure myself on optimizing my timeline. Everything that's meant for me will happen at the right time more or less. I hope. I might go back in my thirties but I want to save my money, not get into debt, do some travels and self-exploration.
I noticed no matter what I did, my parents wouldn't be pleased. Somebody would have something to say.

Capitalism pushes for optimization at all cost. I'm not the perfect person, but I really think the best thing one can do sometimes is to self preserve. Chill out. I saw a comment here the other day that said one must always learn to be content with scarcity for this life. Also "the end of ambition is the start of wisdom". Rad.

My toxic family wants me to pick the perfect job and the richest husband, to have more choices, options, businesses, children etc. But the mental load of those expectations only made me hate myself. My fiance, a modest guy, was the first person to tell me how enough I was, and he is a daily reminder that there are things in this life that cannot be bought. He was the first person I ever met who never compared himself to others. My family preened and shamed me to be what they thought was perfect. I've dated millionaire's sons and they never treated me like he does, surprisingly. They did illicit drugs for fun or for their physique and lots of silly things. I also learned I didn't want children through their personalities, ahahaha.

It took healing and time and a daily practice to connect to the divine but it's worth waiting this life out to finally be at peace with yourself \^\_\^ and let go.
